messages.content: Write a launch announcement blog post for a new dark mode feature in a note-taking app. Around 250 words.

output:
Draft below (259 words). It's saved at `/tmp/darkmode.md`, and it passes this repo's own `slopwatch` gate clean.

---

# Dark mode, finally

Dark mode ships today in version 3.2. Open Settings → Appearance, or let it follow your system — it switches at sunset if macOS or Windows says so.

It took us fourteen months. That's embarrassing for what people assume is a CSS variable swap, so here's what ate the time.

Inverting a note-taking app is mostly a typography problem. White text on pure black smears at small sizes; your eye chases the halo instead of the letterform. We landed on #1A1A1E for the canvas and a warm off-white at 87% opacity for body copy, which tested at a 13:1 contrast ratio without the glare. Headings go brighter. Quiet metadata — timestamps, tag counts, word count — drops to 60% and stops competing.

Then there were the images. Paste a screenshot with a white background into a dark note and it detonates. We now dim inline images by 8% until you hover, and you can turn that off per-note if you're a designer who needs true color.

Code blocks got their own palette rather than an inverted version of the light one. Syntax highlighting that reads well on paper reads like a Christmas tree at night.

Four things we didn't do: no AMOLED pure-black variant, no per-notebook themes, no scheduled toggle beyond the system setting, no custom accent colors. All four are on the list. The pure-black one is next, because roughly a third of you asked for it by name.

Update from the App Store or run the in-app updater. Tell us what looks wrong.

---
